newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS - EOE call writers rush to buy back.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - EOE call writers rush to buy back.

text.p: Dutch calls traded extensively on Friday in the lead-up to the expiry of options contracts as market makers tried to close positions, dealers said.
"We've seen three times as many calls as puts, almost all of it short-covering" one trader said.
Dealers said a number of market makers had written calls for retail investors, typically Nov 600 AEX calls, some weeks ago.

Wall Street's brief early dip on Thursday had convinced the writers of the viability of their position, but a later rally lifted the AEX well clear of 600 on Friday. Within half an hour of the opening, the index had hit a record high of 611.48
At 1615 GMT, the AEX was up 3.38 points to 608.29.
"A number of people were trying to get the market below 600, but, early on, it was clear there was no chance of that," one trader said.
Data showing United States industrial production fell 0.5 percent against a forecast of a 0.2 percent rise scuppered any hopes that the market might be led down by other exchanges.
Options in individual stocks were subsumed by the general picture. However, financials performed well in the cash market and gave rise to healthy call activity in the stock.
